findings.summary: Subtraction guard condition is inverted, causing u64 underflow when audio bitrate exceeds container bitrate.
findings.mechanism: The task requires computing container_bps - audio_bps only when that leaves a positive value (i.e., container_bps > audio_bps). The code instead guards with `container_bps < audio_bps && audio_bps > 0`, which triggers the subtraction exactly when it would underflow (audio > container), and falls through to the plain `container_bps` in the case where subtraction would actually be safe and correct (container > audio). Since video_stream_bps/audio_bps are u64, container_bps - audio_bps panics on underflow in debug builds and wraps to a huge value in release builds, producing a nonsensical (near-u64::MAX) video bitrate for any file where the video bit_rate field is absent and audio bitrate happens to exceed the container total (e.g. slightly stale/misreported ffprobe fields).
